_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::thermo_transient_mms#1 — in 2D the plain 'DESIGN SURF NEUMANN CONDITIONS' on a DSURF covering every node IS the thermo body load, and at most one such condition may touch an element. Three arms on the same manufactured-solution deck: ONE applies the source and the centre node is 'is CORRECT' (exit 0); OVERLAP adds a second DSURF over the same nodes and 4C throws 'more than one VolumeNeumann cond on one node' from src/thermo/src/element/4C_thermo_ele_impl.cpp — during element evaluation, after the discretisation is already built (OVERLAP_BUILT_DISCRETISATION=yes), not at input read; NONE omits the condition entirely and 4C says nothing at all (MISSING_BODY_LOAD_WARNINGS=0), the centre node quietly landing at 8.89e-01 instead of -1.13e-02. The asymmetry is the lesson: a duplicated body load is fatal, a missing one is silent. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: more than one VolumeNeumann cond on one node

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: stop duplicating the condition. The throw vanishes, EXIT_OVERLAP becomes 0 and the fixture must go red.
remove the other half: give the third arm its body load back. It then matches the analytic value, the 8.89e-01 reading disappears and the fixture must go red.
